record_notes.DCP-LETT-1923: July 10, 1856 Hooker ALS; all sixteen blocks, exclusions, annotations, sixteen notes and bibliography read. Salter Epilobium seed-grown result appears ordinary roseum, undermining alleged hybrid; Henslow Aegilops sport remains qualified. First 112 Forbes pages offered, not yet Darwin receipt. Huxley response read after weekend visit, distinguished from original lecture and Falconer Paris boast. Delayed attention to Darwin because father away. Tristan grass from St Paul adds evidence; renewed list search future. Chile/NZ list reviewed, plants not mountain species and genera not remarkable in range. Australian alpine comparisons partly rely on Mueller, not all firsthand Hooker observation. Lyell has not forwarded letter. P13 retracts Viscum hermaphroditism, identifies Aristolochia approximately and promises stigma recheck. P14 variety/intermediate inquiry remains prospective. P16 questions interspecific crossing; Darwin corrects that misunderstanding July 13. Direct source for 1924; also reversely answers 1918, 1919 and 1921 in distinct scopes. Darwin annotations remain undated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1924: July 13 with 1856 supplied; twelve blocks, all apparatus read. P1 first thanks Hooker Huxley evaluation, then quotes a separate Huxley communication and makes the Devil’s chaplain reflection; final portion clarifies crossing within species/close varieties rather than hybrids and reports two or three days of wheat observation qualified by external appearance. Brown stigma-brush question is new. P2 Lemann list lent to Forbes is inferred not returned, not secure possession proof. P3 encloses old Lyallia note and jokes about Vestiges. P4–7 answer Chile/NZ report, multiple centres/Mueller, request Forbes sheets and qualify Henslow result with contamination-distance question. P8 requests manuscript review in five or six weeks, not current delivery. P10 future request disclaimer; P11 Lyell mutation sympathy/permission is Darwin report, P12 hoped Wednesday forwarding not completed. Accepted reply scope excludes unrelated Huxley quotation, old list/enclosure and manuscript request.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1932: July 19 with 1856 supplied, eleven blocks, all apparatus. Explicit thanks for acceptance of manuscript-review request identifies a missing intervening Hooker letter. Plant crossing difficulties, fatal Sweet Pea castration, liquid/dry semen argument and tree sex-separation hypothesis are qualified theory, not established universal law. Proposed NZ comparison lacks standard and is complicated by bushes. Aegilops rarity remarks were new to Darwin and absent from preserved July 10 source. Continental extensions tolerated only hypothetically in a few cases; invitation declined due to bad three weeks, not attended. Emma condition reported. Do not substitute 1923 for missing reply merely because topics continue.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1945: July 26 with month/year supplied, six blocks, all notes/bibliography. ID sorts after August letters but body chronology is July. Lyell has lent Westminster Review; forwarding on Monday is future. Forbes sheets sent a few days ago, proving prior custody rather than exact receipt or complete reading. New Tristan/Kerguelen/Fuegia comparison, water-plant pod flotation inquiry and request for possible Himalayan close-plot list. Thirty-four square feet of lawn yielded eighteen plants in seventeen genera during summer; comparison with Keeling not exact ecological equivalence. Requested seeds/lists are not supplied by the outgoing body.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1933: July 30 with 1856 supplied; seven blocks and eleven notes/bibliography. Missing Hooker letter has value, and Lyell materials enclosed for return. Difference is probability of vast subsidence, not denial of possibility. No distant old-rock example and preliminary mammal-depth comparison support Darwin doubts, not finished survey. Letter from Lyell to Hooker July 25 is discussed as third-party correspondence, with excerpts only in apparatus, not an independently admitted whole incoming letter. Darwin disputes predicted species-name proliferation and geological indifference, speculates about future laws of change. Manuscript not copied before tour; intended appended concession is proposed wording. P1/P3 directly elicit 1937 discussion. Earlier Lyell knowledge already accepted; forwarding does not reset it.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1937: August 4, 1856 Hooker ALS, twelve blocks, complete exclusions/notes/annotations/bibliography. Lyell letters received but not digested. Geologic time-slices, Snowdon and coal-field reasoning questioned. Two supposed new NZ Epacrideae identified with Tasmanian plants; scarcity/alpine sharing against absence of large dominant families underpins argument against migration. Continental extension admitted difficult and incomplete, tentatively preferred rather than certain. P8 hydrostatic pressure speculation distinguishes grand geography from local subsidence. P9 answers mammal argument, P10 explains threat to centres and presents two objections to transmutation. P11 returns Lyell letters and asks about Tyndall cleavage. Undated Darwin pencilled no annotations are not dated August 4 knowledge. Directly answered in 1938 and reversely answers 1933.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1938: August 5 with year supplied; eight blocks and full apparatus. Hooker review received but reading future in opening sentence. Rest P1 responds to Epacrideae/Eucalypti and tentative continental-extension argument, emphasizing unknown dispersal means and value of testing them. P2 island extinction countered by naturalised mammals, Java/Borneo and specific-centre questions not understood, direct climate influence assigned little. P3 kitchen garden/cattle analogy defines centre; Bakewell/Short-Horn historical error is preserved with apparatus correction, not silently fixed in target text. P4 gratitude and self-doubt. P5 Austen not read attentively; Tyndall read and has changed cleavage opinion, but movement qualification persists. P6 revised foliation view. P7 tour wish, P8 manuscript not ready until return. Direct response to 1937 mainly P1 after review receipt through P6, including explicit Austen/Tyndall questions omitted by worker scope.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1940: August 7 with year supplied; five blocks and full apparatus. Tristan manuscript received and promised return, but not yet studied; some plants unknown to Hooker. Antarctic cases difficult even for extensions; supports possibility of iceberg seed transport, not demonstrated transport for each species. Seeks comparative representative American species in Tristan versus Kerguelen. P5 has read HALF Hooker review, unlike August 5 receipt and October 9 retrospective full reading. Current covering letter/list not transcribed; July 10 promise is not an equivalent received list.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1950: September 8 with year supplied, five blocks and full footnotes/bibliography. Missing September 1 Hooker letter received this morning, explicit September 8 receipt. Swiss pedestrian/glacier reports and Tyndall/Sorby theories discussed, not directly observed by Darwin. Domestic rabbit skeleton comparison and Waterhouse quoted assessment attributed. Requests Vienna Laburnum inquiry; yellow-branch seeds obtained but germination result future. Hooker later writes a separate note on source about one-time coloured flowers and no graft; this is reported in footnote 12, not Charles body nor dated same September 8. His inquiry report/return route remains a supplemental-source lead. Emma sixth-month pregnancy apparatus not all contemporary stated content.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1963: September 28 with year supplied, eleven retained blocks and complete notes/bibliography. Requests ripe named aquatic pods with stalk/leaves for flotation, unsuccessful attempts to obtain two wide-ranging species. Address block to Acton/Post Office/Bromley has literal diag/ramme extraction damage. Promises difficult geographical-distribution manuscript in weeks; not yet delivered. Hopes meet October 16; later minutes confirming attendance remain later evidence. Footnote says missing list, while body does not securely establish a new separate enclosed list; do not reconstruct one.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1969: October 5 with year supplied, seven blocks and all notes. Requests seeds via George Snow/Nag’s Head/Borough, explicitly a different safer/slower route from water pods; seeds not yet received and identity unclear. Address formatting raw diag/ramme held. Cytisus inquiry results judged too weak; Darwin pleased to disbelieve a rate of change that would be too fast, not general denial of species change. Preserved September 8 outgoing and its later Hooker note are not automatically a full current incoming reply. No identified whole prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1971: October 9 with year supplied, four blocks and full apparatus. Does not remember a recent list; requests named marsh/water pods, having tested sixty or seventy other capsules for flotation. Upcoming London October 15–18 and proposed seed delivery are plans, not already fulfilled. P4 says review read long ago, a retrospective bound distinct from August 5 receipt and August 7 half reading. Missing Hooker inquiry cannot be replaced by Darwin earlier request.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1965: One-page unsigned Darwin covering note, six blocks, salutation and both notes read. All October 16, 1856 supplied from intended Philosophical Club meeting; hand delivery is likely editorial reconstruction, while posting is admitted possible. Manuscript completed October 13 and read by Hooker November 9, but that does not establish exact delivery day. Requests botanical accuracy, broad/marginal criticism and restraint with unfinished assumptions. Manuscript fragment and back-page notes exist elsewhere but are not transcribed here; covering note is not full chapter or prompt. Retain exact-day review hold despite singleton XML.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1918: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Morning July 5, supplied 1856, four blocks and complete apparatus. Brief thanks for interesting note before post closes; substantive new request to re-examine marked Tristan list and Fuegian/circumpolar relations. Actual list and red crosses are unavailable here. No Lyell route occurs in the body; editorial summary belongs to evening 1919. Generic thanks alone does not justify a separate fully scoped training reply. Morning precedes 1919 by its explicit internal reference.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1919: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Evening July 5, supplied 1856, all thirteen blocks, notes and bibliography. P1 develops Tristan/Antarctic-continent question from morning letter. P2 acknowledges Lyell long reply, P3 requests forwarding of Darwin’s letter, which is not yet established as done. P4–10 directly answer 1911: Flora/Laburnum translation and follow-up, Entada establishment, Aristolochia/Viscum and stigma readiness, parthenogenesis, Aldrovanda with remembered Candolle parallel, and Ray Society policy based on own Cirripedia experience. P11 £20 is pledge, not February 1857 recorded payment. P13 asks for intermediate-variety examples after Wollaston; other subject and missing prior cases. Editorial summary belongs to morning 1918. Receipt of Hooker note some days ago is relative, not an exact date. Lyell source is a journal extract of missing original, so known-by acknowledgement does not prove every retained diagram or unsent postscript was received.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1921: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. July 8, supplied 1856, six blocks and complete apparatus. Darwin discovers previously scored Tristan passage he had forgotten and partly withdraws request; this is rereading, not first receipt. Chile–New Zealand subset copied from Hooker list, with habitat/range questions; full underlying and copied lists not transcribed. P5 began rereading Galápagos paper last night, July 7, not a completed reread. Lyell verdict still unclear. No distinctive surviving current Hooker input established for a direct pair.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
